description:
FILED s452ab (Opus, round 11 agent AB), found when #733 made t/op/filetest.t
run a SKIP block that had never executed.  PRE-EXISTING and general.

A perl filename is a literal string.  SBCL's pathname parser reads `*` (and
the other wildcard characters) as a WILD component, so any PCL path operation
on such a name dies instead of touching the file:

    my $n = "/tmp/pcl_star_*_probe";
    open my $fh, ">", $n or print "openfail: $!\n";
    close $fh if $fh;
    print "exists=", (-e $n ? 1 : 0), "\n";
    unlink $n;
        perl: exists=1 / done          (the file is created and removed)
        PCL:  dies -- "Can't find the truename of wild pathname
              #<pathname ... :NAME #<sb-impl::pattern :multi-char-wild ...>>"

WHERE IT BIT: t/op/filetest.t's `SKIP: { use Perl::OSType 'os_type'; if
(os_type ne 'Unix') { skip "Not Unix", 3 } ... }` block.  Until #733 the
bareword `os_type` was the STRING "os_type", so the condition was true and
the block SKIPPED; now it runs, reaches `system 'ln','-s',$f,\*foo` and
`-l \*foo` (perl's rule: a non-bareword argument to -l is a FILE NAME, so the
glob stringifies to `*main::foo` and that IS the file name), and dies on the
`*`.  The file moved 183/251 -> 181/250 as a result -- three `skip` rows that
counted as passes replaced by an honest abort two rows earlier.  s438h's
lesson again: a fix that makes values real exposes what was passing on
nothing.

FIX SHAPE (not designed): every place the runtime turns a perl filename into
a CL pathname must go through one helper that escapes the wildcard characters
(`sb-impl::` has `unparse-native-namestring` / the `parse-native-namestring`
family, which does NOT interpret wildcards -- that is almost certainly the
right primitive, and it is ONE seam, not per-builtin).  Rule 11: find every
caller first -- open, unlink, -X, stat/lstat, rename, symlink, opendir,
truename -- and route them all, or the next filename with a `*` finds the one
that was missed.

BAR: the probe above; a filename with `?`, `[`, `]` and a literal `~`; the
same names through open/-e/-l/unlink/rename/stat/opendir; t/op/filetest.t
back to at least 183 verified rows; a full sweep leg (this is `cl/**`).


PROMOTED s452 (Fable, AB ask 1 accepted): NOT a filler -- a general runtime gap on legal perl filenames (ONE seam, parse-native-namestring; every open/filetest/unlink on a name containing a wildcard char dies).  HEADS the next round.  Fix shape to evaluate first: route filename->pathname conversion through sb-ext:parse-native-namestring with :as-directory handling or wrap names in an escaping layer at the ONE conversion seam (grep for the existing filename->pathname helper -- rule 11: there should be exactly one; if there are several, that is the first finding).  Bar: open/read/write/unlink/filetest/-e on names with * ? [ ] { } ~ vs perl; op/filetest.t recovers its 2 aborted rows (181/250 -> 183/251-ish, re-splice); glob() semantics UNCHANGED (glob is where wildcards are MEANT to expand).  COMPLETED s454ad, merged + reviewed s455 (round-12 merge review): probes identical to perl, guards pass; #755 gained a Fable review fix on top (ea58eb4, readdir literal names) + task #800 (glob output twin).
subject: a filename containing a wildcard character dies in SBCL's pathname parser; perl filenames are literal strings
